items.scenario: Checkout p95 and JDBC borrow wait rise together while traffic, heap, GC pause, and CPU remain near baseline.
items.prompt: Rank the database-pool and JVM-memory hypotheses, and name the evidence required before intervention.
items.answer: Prioritize connection-pool contention because borrow wait temporally explains request latency while memory indicators do not deteriorate first. Confirm pool occupancy by service, worker wait state, request trace, database backtrace, caller volume, and business success before selecting a bounded mitigation.
items.explanation: Correlation across a shared time window is stronger than a single elevated heap percentage. The leading signal and causal path must agree.

items.scenario: A checkout timeout log and an export progress log occur one second apart but have different correlation identifiers.
items.prompt: Explain what can and cannot be concluded from those records.
items.answer: The timestamps support a shared incident window but do not prove that one execution caused the other. Correlate checkout traces, pool metrics, database backtraces, export concurrency, and change history; preserve both identifiers so each path remains auditable.
items.explanation: Temporal proximity is a hypothesis generator, not causal proof. Service-flow and resource evidence connect the workloads.

items.scenario: A custom job saturates database connections. An operator proposes terminating database sessions directly.
items.prompt: Select a safe containment sequence under the managed public-cloud responsibility model.
items.answer: Declare the incident, preserve evidence, stop or abort the customer-owned abortable workload through supported administration, protect ambiguous transactions, observe drain and recovery, and contact SAP Support if managed-database intervention is still required. Do not teach direct database session termination as a customer capability.
items.explanation: The customer controls custom workload behavior; direct managed-database intervention crosses the responsibility boundary.

items.scenario: An alert fires only when checkout p95 exceeds 15 seconds. It has no business success, traffic, pool, or change-event context.
items.prompt: Redesign the alert and diagnostic dashboard so it is actionable without encoding a synthetic metric name as a universal SAP default.
items.answer: Define a journey SLI and environment-specific thresholds from baseline; pair latency with error and success rates, traffic, pool occupancy and wait, workers, database contribution, dependency latency, and change events. Link a runbook and preserve the diagnostic window. Validate names and retention against the subscription.
items.explanation: An actionable alert identifies impact and supplies discriminating evidence. Product availability does not establish universal thresholds or retention.
items.applicableVersion: SAP Commerce Cloud public cloud 2211; metric names and retention subscription-dependent

items.scenario: The export job is stopped and checkout p95 falls, but three payment authorizations lack confirmed orders.
items.prompt: Define the minimum recovery evidence before incident closure.
items.answer: Verify sustained pool headroom and borrow wait, checkout latency/error/success under representative traffic, synthetic end-to-end order behavior, no resumed export, and controlled reconciliation of each authorization using idempotent business rules. Assign owners and an elevated-monitoring window.
items.explanation: Performance recovery does not resolve divergent external business state. Closure needs technical and transaction evidence.

items.scenario: Engineering will repair the export job before re-enabling it.
items.prompt: Design the performance and failure tests that must gate reactivation.
items.answer: Use production-shaped data and traffic; vary worker count, page size, schedule overlap, and cancellation; assert bounded pool use and borrow wait, checkout SLOs, transaction duration, progress and restart semantics, no duplicate export, abort behavior, and retained traces. Test on the target update line without claiming simulation results are platform execution.
items.explanation: A successful export is insufficient if it consumes shared capacity or cannot be contained safely.
items.applicableVersion: SAP Commerce Cloud public cloud 2211; execute against selected update line
